Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{PS}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{SQ}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{TS}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{RT}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{QT}$ in terms of $a,b,c,$ and $d.$ To denote the corresponding vectors, use $a$, $b,$ $c,$ and $d.$

$\overset{\to }{QT}=$ 
 {{field-1}}
worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $Q$ to $T$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{QT}=\overset{\to }{QS}+\overset{\to }{ST},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/cd8dc0d2e01927c8b2ca116265b257d835a1baae62272b703610f2947d92a8c2.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{QS}=-b,\,\overset{\to }{ST}=-c.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073669/assets/8ed8c71e0d45ae0c9cf7d8a7d2889ee3a79471aaeb408ad0f53f487523daac13.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{QT} & =\overset{\to }{QS}+\overset{\to }{ST} \\  & =-b+(-c) \\  & =-b-c.\end{aligned}
$$
